transcript.content: Hi, welcome in — I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?
I’ve been feeling wound up almost all day. It’s like my body is bracing for something, even when I’m just sitting at my computer or trying to relax after dinner.
How long have you been feeling this constant sense of being wound up or on edge — days, weeks, or longer?
It’s been about thirteen months now—since my sister in Arecibo started needing a lot more help from the family.

Is this constant sense of being on edge mainly focused on your sister's situation, or do you find yourself worrying excessively about several different things in your life—like work, health, or other family matters?

It’s not just my sister. My mind jumps from one thing to another—something I may have missed at the office, my husband driving home, church commitments, bills. I’m always sort of preparing for a problem that hasn’t even happened.
Along with this constant worrying, have you noticed physical symptoms like muscle tension, feeling easily tired, trouble concentrating, irritability, or difficulty sleeping?

I have been more irritable. I’m usually pretty patient, but lately small things get to me—like a late update in a documentation meeting, someone singing off-tempo at choir, or people asking me too many questions while I’m cooking on Sunday. I answer sharper than I mean to.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep, like trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or feeling rested when you wake up?

Most nights I can fall asleep eventually, but I wake up around three or four. Then I’m thinking about my sister’s next appointment or some server issue at work. Even if I get enough hours, I wake up feeling like I never really rested.
Have you noticed any physical tension, like tightness in your neck, shoulders, or jaw, or feeling physically restless during this time?
Yes. I feel wound up almost all day, like my body is bracing for something. Even when I’m just sitting at my computer or trying to relax after dinner, I can’t quite settle down.
Have you noticed any trouble concentrating or your mind going blank because of all this worrying?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed my mind going blank, exactly.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports excessive, uncontrollable worry about multiple domains (work, family, health, finances) lasting over 13 months, more days than not, accompanied by muscle tension/restlessness, irritability, non-restorative sleep with early waking, and subjective fatigue. Worry is not confined to a single stressor (sister's illness) but generalizes across life areas, and symptoms have persisted well beyond the 6-month threshold, supporting Generalized Anxiety Disorder over an Adjustment Disorder. No manic, psychotic, or panic-specific symptoms reported, and concentration difficulty/mind going blank was not endorsed, but sufficient criteria (irritability, sleep disturbance, muscle tension, restlessness) are met for diagnosis.
